Mailgun lowered free-tier from 10k to 625 emails/month; inbound mail no longer supported on the free plan at all, which users found disappointing.
"batch and switch from 10,000 to 625 is worthy of never using them ever again."
User used Mailgun's inbound routing checkbox to forward mail to another address for years; losing that on the free tier "completely wrecks my use-case for mailgun."
"We have used Mailgun to power our SaaS emails for years with great deliverability and without paying a cent. It makes sense for them to charge for their service."
User compared costs: moved from Mailgun to SES because SES pricing is far cheaper (60K free emails from AWS instance) with deliverability on par, though SES lacks Mailgun's analytics.
Long-time free-tier user struggled with Mailgun DNS validation dashboard reporting unresolved problems with no details, and free-tier support couldn't help diagnose it.
"I moved to mailgun after the mandrill 'incident' and I have been very happy since. I hope the service will stay stable!"
"Mailgun's a solid service. They've got the best inbound handling of all of the services out there in terms of letting you apply rules before the messages hit your servers."

User with deliverability issues on Office365 contacted Mailgun support about a dedicated IP; support refused payment and switched them to a better sending server within hours, resolving junk-folder issues.
"As a developer it's incredibly easy to integrate with, the dashboards are very helpful for debugging... I've found their competitors to be harder to integrate with and focused more on mass mailing."
"I agree, Mailgun is fantastic. However, their lack for 2 factor authentication is seriously worrying."
"Happy Mailgun user here. Sending 1MM+ transactional emails/month and 9MM+ marketing emails/month. Working flawlessly, given that you setup everything correctly (separate domains, dedicated IPs...)."
"I used to use Postmark but switched to Mailgun. I'm very happy." — user asked what advantage Postmark had over Mailgun, suggesting satisfaction after switching.
"I'm a big fan of mailgun. It is far better than mandril, sendgrid and probably ses - without a lot of the set up."
"Mailgun's logging is great, and includes the full-text of messages."

"The reason why we use Mailgun is to avoid deploying and maintaining e-mail infrastructure which is very hard and high cost. We would rather keep paying Mailgun about $20/mo as this is cheaper by several magnitudes than the self-hosting option."
